items.name: full
items.prompt:
You are a YouTube retention analyst. Watch this ENTIRE video with sound, start to finish. Context: PBS Eons (English, ~8 min, 3.9M views). Write in English unless told otherwise.

PART A - VERBATIM SCRIPT. Transcribe every spoken word of the narration, in order, as timestamped lines "[mm:ss] text". Keep each line to 1-2 sentences. If the narration is Hindi, write the Hindi line in Devanagari and then " || " and an English translation on the same line. After each line add a short bracket with what is on screen at that moment: visual type (3D render / 2D animation / stock footage / photo / map / chart), any on-screen text word for word, and what moves. Note music changes and sound effects as their own lines like "[mm:ss] (SFX: ...)". Do not summarise or skip any narration.

PART B - STRUCTURE. A table: start, end, segment purpose, the open question or promise that is active, the payoff delivered (if any).

PART C - WHY IT HOLDS VIEWERS. Be specific and quote exact lines:
1. The hook: the exact words of the first 30 seconds, what promise or question it plants, and when (timestamp) the viewer is first rewarded.
2. Payoff rhythm: list every "wow" fact or reveal with its timestamp; give the average seconds between them.
3. Pattern interrupts: how often the visual changes (cuts or new graphics per minute), and the main tricks used.
4. Scale comparisons: every comparison to a familiar thing (buildings, mountains, people), with timestamps.
5. Characters, humour, questions to the viewer, cliffhangers: list them with timestamps.
6. Narration: approximate words per minute, tone, and voice style.
7. The ending: last 30 seconds word for word, how they ask for subscribe/like, and whether they tease another video.
8. Title and thumbnail promise: what the title and thumbnail promise and the timestamp where the video delivers it.

Be exhaustive in PART A. Accuracy matters more than brevity.
